title: Hand of Straights
prompt:
Given an integer array `hand` of card values and an integer `groupSize`, return whether the cards can be rearranged into groups of exactly `groupSize` **consecutive** values.

**Example**: `hand = [1,2,3,6,2,3,4,7,8]`, `groupSize = 3` → `true` (`[1,2,3],[2,3,4],[6,7,8]`).

**Constraints**: `1 ≤ hand.length ≤ 10^4`, `1 ≤ groupSize ≤ hand.length`.
hints: Look at the smallest card in the hand. What must its role be in whatever group it ends up in?
It must START a group (nothing smaller can come before it). Build that group right away, then repeat with the new smallest card. Keep counts in sorted order so the smallest is easy to find.
Use a `TreeMap` of counts. Take `firstKey()` and decrement `first .. first + groupSize - 1`, returning false if any is missing. Quick reject: `hand.length % groupSize != 0`.

solution.explanation: The smallest remaining card can only be the first card of a run, so the run it starts is forced. Forming it greedily never rules out a valid arrangement. Repeating on what remains either uses every card or finds a gap. O(n log n) time for the TreeMap operations, O(n) space.
